expectations.text: Does NOT endorse rewriting the hot paths in Rust (as microservices) as the next step on the evidence given.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "No, it isn't the obvious call." ... "A separate Rust microservice is justified mainly for organizational or scaling reasons... Speed on one endpoint isn't one of those reasons." ... "profile before you rewrite." | grader 2: "No, it isn't the obvious call." and "A separate Rust microservice is justified mainly for organizational or scaling reasons... Speed on one endpoint isn't one of those reasons."

expectations.text: Challenges the premise that Python / the language is the bottleneck.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "nothing you've said shows yet that Python is the bottleneck. A Django dashboard endpoint at 800ms p95 is almost never slow because of the language." plus the 15%-CPU arithmetic showing an infinitely fast rewrite only reaches ~680ms. | grader 2: "Why 'Python is too slow' is doubtful" section and "nothing you've said shows yet that Python is the bottleneck... If Python CPU time is 15% of your 800ms, an infinitely fast Rust rewrite gets you to about 680ms."

expectations.text: Recommends profiling or measuring first (e.g. finding N+1 queries, slow DB queries, serialization, or external calls).
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Get a breakdown of where the time goes. Use your APM ... Run `py-spy` against a production worker ... Run `django-silk` or debug-toolbar locally to count queries." and lists N+1 queries, missing indexes, external HTTP calls, serialization. | grader 2: "Get a breakdown of where the time goes... Run py-spy against a production worker... Run django-silk or debug-toolbar locally to count queries."

expectations.text: States concrete conditions under which a rewrite or a native (e.g. Rust) component WOULD be justified.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "If profiling shows most of the wall time is Python CPU in a specific hot function, and it's real computation that can't move into SQL or be solved with a better algorithm, then native code makes sense." plus the PyO3/maturin extension option and the 'strongest case against my view' section (team knows Rust, several CPU-heavy paths, DB already ruled out). | grader 2: "If profiling shows most of the wall time is Python CPU in a specific hot function... then native code makes sense... Write a Rust extension module with PyO3/maturin that runs inside the Django process." plus the organizational-reasons paragraph and the 'strongest case against my view' section.

expectations.text: Gives a clear bottom-line verdict rather than an unresolved "it depends".
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Bottom line: profile before you rewrite... I'd bet it's queries or caching, not Rust." | grader 2: "Bottom line: profile before you rewrite. Come back with the time breakdown... and the right move will be obvious. I'd bet it's queries or caching, not Rust."
